access.name: How players get in
access.hint: With tokens: the server checks a token that a GM's browser signs for each player, from the app id and secret below; it needs token authentication and Prosody's presence_identity module (see the module's README). Open server: anyone with the room link joins, as on a fresh Jitsi install, and Foundry tells everyone who each player is. People who aren't in this world can still join an open room if they know its link.

serverUrl.name: Jitsi server address
serverUrl.hint: Your Jitsi Meet server, such as https://meet.example.com. For an open server, paste the room link you would send to friends, such as https://meet.example.com/OurTable (letters, digits, - and _ in the room name); without a room, a random one is added. Plain http:// works only on this computer or a private network. Every player can read this setting.

xmppDomain.name: XMPP domain
xmppDomain.hint: Leave empty when it is the server's host name. Docker installs of Jitsi use meet.jitsi.

mucDomain.name: Conference domain
mucDomain.hint: Leave empty for conference.<XMPP domain>. Docker installs of Jitsi use muc.meet.jitsi.

appId.name: Jitsi app id
appId.hint: The server's JWT_APP_ID. Stored only in this browser. Players get short-lived tokens from a GM's browser.

appSecret.name: Jitsi app secret
appSecret.hint: The server's JWT_APP_SECRET. Stored only in this browser and never sent to players. Enter it on each browser a GM uses to run the game.

notices.outsider: Someone in the Jitsi room isn't in this world. They get no place in the call here, but they can see and hear it. Keep the room link private.
notices.tokenRemoved: A sign-in token was taken out of the Jitsi server address: every player can read that setting.
